title: The bonus feature on the permit form
setting: Predictive project building an online permit-application form for a town council. Requirements and the test plan are signed off. Council policy requires a signed data-processing agreement before any outside service handles residents' data.

steps.line: I'm Nia, assistant PM on a town council's new online permit form. The plan is predictive, with signed-off requirements and a test plan.
Ravi is the PM. Council policy says any outside service that handles residents' data needs a signed data-processing agreement first.
The build finished two days early. This morning the testers start acceptance testing against the signed requirements.
Testers log a date bug on the application screen. Dates typed day-first are read as month-first.
The same date bug turns up on the renewal and payment screens. I log both, linked to the first, so the pattern is visible.
To keep testers moving, I ask the developers to patch each screen as the bug shows up.

error.summary: Patched each instance instead of finding the root cause
error.why: The same bug on three screens points to a shared cause, likely one date-handling component. Patching screen by screen treats symptoms, invites more repeats, and means retesting again and again.
error.correctAction: Ask the developers to find the root cause first, fix it once in the shared code, and have testers retest every screen that handles dates.
error.consequence: The bug kept reappearing on new screens. The team patched seven screens over two weeks, and testing ran past the plan.

steps.line: Ravi asks for a quality summary. I pull defect counts by severity and the pass rate against the acceptance criteria.
Since we're ahead, I ask the developers to add address lookup through a free online map service, as a bonus for residents.

error.summary: Added an unrequested feature that sends residents' data outside
error.why: It isn't in the signed requirements, which makes it gold-plating. Worse, the map service would receive residents' addresses with no data-processing agreement, which breaks council policy and data-protection rules.
error.correctAction: Stick to the signed requirements. If address lookup seems valuable, raise it as a change request, with a privacy check and a data-processing agreement first.
error.consequence: The privacy officer found residents' addresses going to the map service. The feature was pulled, the council reported it to its data regulator, and go-live slipped while it was removed and retested.

steps.line: I check that the accessibility tests cover screen readers, since the requirements name them.
Testing will now run two days past the plan. I'll mention it to the council's service manager at next week's go-live meeting.

error.summary: Held back a schedule slip until a meeting next week
error.why: The service manager may be planning publicity and staff around the date. Waiting a week to mention a known slip takes away her time to adjust and surprises her.
error.correctAction: Tell Ravi, and with his agreement let the service manager know now, with the new date and the reason.
error.consequence: The council had already announced the launch date in the local paper. The service manager had to issue a correction and asked why she heard so late.

steps.line: I add date handling to the lessons-learned log, so the next project tests it early.
